redFlags.source: Wikipedia, 1998 Belgian Grand Prix: 'The race was stopped before the end of the first lap', stopped within the first two laps so 'a full restart over the original distance would take place', 'The second attempt to start the race took place nearly an hour after the first', 'The safety car was withdrawn at the end of the second lap' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_Belgian_Grand_Prix); L. Smith, '1998 Belgian GP: When the Schumachers went to war', Autosport (reprint 22 Jul 2025): 'The rules at the time meant the start was voided', 'the second start' (https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/1998-belgian-gp-when-the-schumachers-went-to-war/10744117/); Wikipedia, 'List of red-flagged Formula One races' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_red-flagged_Formula_One_races): lap 1, code Y (restarted over the original distance)
redFlags.note: A voided start, not a suspension: the race was run again from a second standing start over the full 44 laps (no source says 'standing' in so many words; both describe a second start from the grid, as all 1998 starts were). Jolpica's 44 laps are the restarted race only, with no stoppage lap, so this entry has no resumeLap; laps 1-2 of the restarted race ran behind the SC (Hakkinen/Herbert at La Source). Barrichello, Panis, Salo and Rosset did not take the second start.
